title: Quantification of Phytoplankton Cells with Preys Using Flow Cytometry
author: Valeria Jimenez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be2vjge6

steps.title: Prepare Prey Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the prey (YG-beads or FLBs) stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate the solution for approximately 60 seconds.

steps.title: Prepare Fixative Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary fixatives under a hood.

substeps.instruction: Prepare acid Lugol's iodine solution: Dissolve 10 g of Potassium iodide in 100 ml distilled water, slowly add 5 g of iodine crystals and shake to dissolve, then add 10 ml glacial acetic acid and store in the dark.
Prepare sodium thiosulfate solution: Add 3 ml of sodium thiosulfate to 97 ml of distilled water.

steps.title: Inoculate Phytoplankton with Prey
steps.instruction: Add preys to phytoplankton flasks (at least 2 to 3 replicates per strain and culture condition) to achieve a prey-to-cell ratio of 1 to 2.

substeps.instruction: Add preys to each flask one at a time.
Gently mix the flask to evenly distribute microspheres.

steps.title: Sample and Fix Cultures
steps.instruction: Collect and fix samples at specific time points (T0, T20, and T40). This can be done in the culture flask or by taking an aliquot (e.g., 5 ml) into a culture tube or scintillation vial.

substeps.instruction: Take a sub-sample immediately after prey addition for T0 background correction.
Take subsequent samples after 20 minutes (T20) and 40 minutes (T40) of incubation.
Fix each 5 ml sample as follows: Add 50 µl of acid Lugol’s iodine solution, then add 300 µl of 37% Formaldehyde, and finally add 50 µl of 3% Thiosulfate.
If the sample is not thoroughly cleared of Lugol’s stain, add additional sodium thiosulfate (e.g., another 50 µl) until clear.

steps.title: Store and Run Samples
steps.instruction: Keep fixed samples on ice in the dark and run them in the flow cytometer on the same day.

steps.title: Analyze Flow Cytometry Data
steps.instruction: Quantify the percentage of cells containing prey and the total prey concentration.

substeps.instruction: Set the threshold on red fluorescence: cells with both red autofluorescence (chlorophyll) and green fluorescence (matching the signal of YG-beads or FLBs) are identified as cells containing prey.
Set the threshold on green fluorescence to confirm the total concentration of prey added to each flask.
